verification.heading: Verification pass — September 25, 2026
verification.markdown:
Checked 2026-09-25 by verification agent (sweep #2). Laws cited as of Sep 2026. **Method note:** WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted). Job 1 was done by primary-host fetch, not search. It relied on the bracketed history line (session-law citations through 2026) of every cited RCW/WAC section on app.leg.wa.gov, the 2026 session-law PDFs those lines link to, the State Building Code Council home page, and the L&I and AG pages.
- **Licensing, RCW 18.27.040 / .050 / .020:** RE-CONFIRMED. The bond is "$30,000 if the applicant is a general contractor or $15,000 if the applicant is a specialty contractor" (history ends 2023 c 213 s 3). Insurance is $50,000 property / $100,000 one person / $200,000 more than one person (last amended 2001). Unregistered work is a gross misdemeanor (last amended 2007). None of these sections has a 2025 or 2026 amendment. Sources: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=18.27.040 ; https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=18.27.050 ; https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=18.27.020. Evidence class GOV.
- **Specialties, WAC 296-200A-016:** RE-CONFIRMED verbatim. Masonry: "This specialty also includes chimney cleaning and repair". The Wood/pellet and gas stove specialty is as quoted in §1. The last filing is WSR 09-10-079 (eff. 6/5/09). Source: https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx?cite=296-200A-016. Evidence class GOV.
- **Seller disclosure, RCW 64.06.020 (Form 17):** RE-CONFIRMED, and Sep-15 blocker 4 is RESOLVED.
  - Statutory numbering: 4.F "Are there any defects with the following" lists "Chimneys"; 5.C asks about wood burning appliances, with the EPA-certification follow-up; 5.E covers CO alarms.
  - The Sep-15 blocker guessed "5.A heating" for the wood-burning item; it is actually 5.C.
  - **New 2026 findings:** 2026 c 194 (ESHB 1500, eff. June 11, 2026) amends only the common-interest-community audit item. 2026 c 173 s 20 (SHB 2239) adds "Does the property include a family burial ground, mausoleum, or columbarium?", effective Jan 1, 2027. Neither changes the chimney, wood-burning or CO items.
  - RCW 64.06.010 (waiver; last amended 2010) and RCW 64.06.030 (3-business-day rescission; last amended 1996) are unchanged.
  - The NWMLS Form 17 is a private form reproducing the statute, and the statutory form is the controlling text.
  - Sources: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=64.06.020 ; https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/biennium/2025-26/Pdf/Bills/Session%20Laws/House/1500-S.SL.pdf ; https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/biennium/2025-26/Pdf/Bills/Session%20Laws/House/2239-S.SL.pdf. Evidence class GOV/DOC.
- **CO law, RCW 19.27.530:** RE-CONFIRMED. Subsection (2)(b) is quoted verbatim in §6. The history is 2012 c 132 s 4 and 2009 c 313 s 2, with no 2025 or 2026 amendment. Source: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=19.27.530. Evidence class GOV.
- **Code cycle, WAC 51-51-003:** RE-CONFIRMED. The 2021 IRC applies, and the last filing is WSR 23-23-104 (eff. 3/16/24). **New finding:** SBCC says "The effective date of the 2024 codes will be May 3, 2027", and the IRC and other packages were filed May 6, 2026, with final adoption targeted for Oct 16, 2026. This is added to §5. Sources: https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx?cite=51-51-003 ; https://sbcc.wa.gov/. Evidence class GOV.
- **WAC 173-433 (Sep-15 blocker 3):** RESOLVED, with a correction.
  - WAC 173-433-100 bars anyone who would "advertise to sell, offer to sell, sell, bargain, exchange, or give away" an uncertified device. It contains no "install" prohibition, so the earlier "illegal to install" claim was wrong and stays out. Limits are 2.5 g/hr for catalytic devices and 4.5 g/hr for all others.
  - WAC 173-433-110 sets opacity at 20% averaged over 6 consecutive minutes in any hour, with a new-fire start-up exception.
  - Both rules were filed as WSR 14-04-013 (eff. 2/23/14).
  - Sources: https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx?cite=173-433-100 ; https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx?cite=173-433-110. Evidence class GOV.
- **Burn bans:** PARTIAL. RCW 70A.15.3580 is re-confirmed: Stage 1 triggers on a forecast above 35 µg/m³; Stage 2 triggers at 25 µg/m³ (24-hour average) with no forecast decline. Its last amendment was 2020 c 20. Agency pages were reached but not their ban wording (see blocker 2). Sources: https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=70A.15.3580 ; https://pscleanair.gov/168 ; https://www.spokanecleanair.org/ ; https://nwcleanairwa.gov/. Evidence class GOV.

- **Consumer Protection Act, RCW 19.86.090:** RE-CONFIRMED. Treble damages may "not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars". The last amendment was 2009. Evidence class GOV.
- **2026 law-change sweep:** done by primary-host fetch, not search. Changes found:
  - 64.06.020 amendments (2026 c 194, 2026 c 173; neither touches hearth items).
  - The SBCC 2024-code effective date of May 3, 2027.
  - No 2025 or 2026 change to RCW 18.27, 19.27.530, 63.14.154, 19.86.090, 70A.15.3580, WAC 296-200A-016 or WAC 173-433.

- **Mirror spot-check:** n/a (Washington is not a mirror state; everything was read on app.leg.wa.gov).
- **Dead links:** none. Every RCW/WAC URL in the file resolved on Sep 25, as did lni.wa.gov/news-events/article/25-23 and atg.wa.gov/home-improvement-scams. That AG page does not mention chimneys; it is cited only as general guidance.

sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; registration, not a license)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; registration, not a license
sections.markdown: **Washington has no license for chimney work — it has registration.** Under the **Contractor Registration Act, RCW ch. 18.27**, anyone who contracts to improve real property for pay must **register with the Dept. of Labor & Industries (L&I)** as a general or specialty contractor — chimney masonry, relining, rebuild, and sweeping-for-hire all fall inside "contractor." L&I's specialty list (**WAC 296-200A-016**) even names the trade: the **Masonry** specialty "also includes chimney cleaning and repair," and a separate **Wood/pellet and gas stove** specialty "installs wood, pellet, or gas stoves, zero clearance and fire place inserts." Registration attests **money, not skill**: per **RCW 18.27.040** a general contractor files a **$30,000 continuous surety bond** ($15,000 specialty), carries liability insurance (RCW 18.27.050: $100,000 per person / $200,000 per occurrence for bodily injury and $50,000 property damage), and holds a UBI number — **there is no competency exam** for general-contractor registration. Public lookup: **secure.lni.wa.gov / "Verify a Contractor"** (lni.wa.gov). Advertising, bidding, or working as a contractor while unregistered is a **gross misdemeanor** (RCW 18.27.020; some violations are also infractions under RCW 18.27.200), and an unregistered contractor cannot sue to collect (RCW 18.27.080). *(Confirm any city add-on registrations — see §5.)*

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: The gap here is unusually clean: L&I registration is a **bond-and-insurance filing with no test at all** for a general contractor, so "registered, bonded, and insured" — the phrase every WA contractor uses — says nothing about whether the person can read a flue. Verifying "licensed and bonded" in WA means confirming an **active L&I registration + bond**, not a passed exam. Individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) remain the only competence signal.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — high confidence; real named chimney/stove line)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; real named chimney/stove line
sections.markdown: **RCW ch. 64.06 requires the seller to deliver the "Form 17" Seller Disclosure Statement** within 5 business days of mutual acceptance (RCW 64.06.020). It is **actual-knowledge, disclosure-only, not a warranty** — and it names the hearth: the statutory form asks **"Are any of the following kinds of wood burning appliances present at the property?" (woodstove, fireplace insert, pellet stove, fireplace)** and, if yes, **"are all of the (1) woodstoves or (2) fireplace inserts certified by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency as clean burning appliances…?"**; **chimneys** are a listed structural component for defects, and the form asks whether the property has CO alarms, noting the seller's RCW 19.27.530 duty. (Statutory form numbering: chimneys = **4.F** "Are there any defects with the following" under 4. STRUCTURAL; wood burning appliances = **5.C** and CO alarms = **5.E** under 5. SYSTEMS AND FIXTURES. 2026 amendments leave these items unchanged: 2026 c 194 (ESHB 1500, eff. June 11, 2026) changes the common-interest-community audit-report item; 2026 c 173 (SHB 2239) adds a family-burial-ground question effective Jan 1, 2027.) The buyer gets a **statutory 3-business-day right to rescind** after delivery (RCW 64.06.030). Crucially, the buyer **may expressly waive** receipt of the statement (RCW 64.06.010), except that if any answer in the "Environmental" section would be "yes," that section cannot be waived — so the disclosure is real but waivable. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: The **Consumer Protection Act, RCW ch. 19.86**, gives a private action for actual damages, costs, and attorney's fees, with **discretionary treble damages capped at $25,000** (RCW 19.86.090) — a softer multiplier than MA/NJ. Enforced privately and by the AG's Consumer Protection Division. Door-to-door / in-person-solicited installment sales carry a **3-business-day right to cancel under RCW 63.14.154** (Retail Installment Sales Act) — plus the federal FTC cooling-off rule. The door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is the textbook target. Complaints: **atg.wa.gov** (file online) and L&I for the contractor bond.

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (GOV — high confidence; statewide code)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: Washington runs a **statewide code**: the **State Building Code (RCW ch. 19.27)**, with the **2021 IRC adopted as the Washington State Residential Code (WAC 51-51-003), effective March 15, 2024** (latest amendment filing effective March 16, 2024; no 2024-IRC adoption appears in WAC 51-51 as of Sep 2026). **Coming change:** the State Building Code Council says "The effective date of the 2024 codes will be May 3, 2027"; the 2024 IRC/IBC/IMC/IFC/UPC rule packages were filed May 6, 2026 with final adoption targeted for Oct 16, 2026 (sbcc.wa.gov, Sep 2026) — until then the 2021 IRC governs. Chimneys/fireplaces are **IRC Chapter 10 (R1001–R1005)** — a NATIONAL STANDARD carried into state law. Relines, rebuilds, crowns, and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally **permit work**; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not. Cities/counties administer permits locally; verify the local building department.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (GOV — high confidence; includes point of sale)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; includes point of sale
sections.markdown: **RCW 19.27.530** requires CO alarms in all residential occupancies (older owner-occupied single-family legally occupied before July 26, 2009 were phased in) — alarms outside each sleeping area, on each level. Existing owner-occupied single-family homes occupied before July 26, 2009 are exempt — **but for any such home sold on or after July 26, 2009, the seller must equip it with CO alarms per the state building code before the buyer or anyone else may legally occupy it** (RCW 19.27.530(2)(b)); new residential construction was covered by Jan 1, 2011 and all other residential occupancies by Jan 1, 2013 — a genuine point-of-sale duty (stronger than MD/IL, which have none). A permitted chimney or stove job is the natural moment to verify alarms.

sections.rawHeading: 7 · Solid fuel / environmental (GOV — high confidence; the big WA section)
sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; the big WA section
sections.markdown: This is Washington's differentiator. Under the **Washington Clean Air Act, RCW ch. 70A.15**, **no new woodstove may be sold or advertised for sale to a Washington resident unless approved by Ecology (RCW 70A.15.3540)**, and solid fuel burning devices offered for sale must meet WA emission limits (**4.5 g/hr generally, 2.5 g/hr catalytic woodstoves; RCW 70A.15.3530**; definitions at RCW 70A.15.3510). **RCW 70A.15.3580 sets first-stage burn bans** (only EPA-certified or Oregon DEQ Phase II devices may burn when fine particulates are forecast to exceed 35 µg/m³ within 48 hours) **and second-stage bans** (no wood burning at all), with an emergency power-outage exception; **RCW 70A.15.3600** bans burning garbage/treated wood and lets authorities prohibit uncertified devices in areas failing federal fine-particulate standards. Ecology's rule **WAC 173-433-100** adds that "A person must not advertise to sell, offer to sell, sell, bargain, exchange, or give away a solid fuel burning device in Washington unless it has been certified and labeled" under EPA's 40 C.F.R. 60 Subpart AAA, and **WAC 173-433-110** caps smoke at "an average of twenty percent opacity for six consecutive minutes in any one-hour period" (except up to 20 minutes per 4 hours when starting a new fire). *(No "install" prohibition appears in WAC 173-433-100 — do not claim one.)* Enforcement is **STATE (Dept. of Ecology) + LOCAL clean-air agencies**: the **Puget Sound Clean Air Agency** (King/Kitsap/Pierce/Snohomish) issues Stage 1/Stage 2 bans (Stage 2 bars **all** wood burning), **Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency** covers the east, and **Northwest Clean Air Agency** the northwest counties. A **Tacoma-Pierce County** rule adds tighter local limits. *(Agency-level details in this paragraph — counties, Stage 2 scope, Tacoma-Pierce rule — are UNVERIFIED on the agencies' own pages as of Sep 25, 2026; publish only the RCW 70A.15.3580 stage triggers and generic agency names.)* This regime touches sweeping/repair indirectly (creosote, replacement-stove sales) — a real content section, unlike the Midwest states.

sections.rawHeading: 8 · Scam landscape (REF/GOV — partial; pull more before publish)
sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: **L&I's Sept. 8, 2025 release "Don't open your door to fraud: Beware of paving scams…"** warns that "similar schemes promote roof replacement, **chimney repairs** and other home improvement jobs" (https://lni.wa.gov/news-events/article/25-23), and the AG runs Home-Improvement-Scam guidance (atg.wa.gov/home-improvement-scams). No WA-specific *chimney-sweep* enforcement action confirmed yet — **re-run search before publish.**

sections.markdown: Seattle/Puget Sound metro runs **above national** on labor; Spokane and rural east nearer or below national. Regionalize upward for the Seattle ring.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Washington **CONFIRMS the license⇄disclosure inverse-correlation verdict, in its weak-credential form.** WA has **no competency license** — only an L&I bond-and-insurance *registration* with no exam — and, matching the pattern, it pairs that thin front-end credential with a **real, named seller disclosure**: Form 17 asks about the wood stove and fireplace insert by name (RCW 64.06), and the sale even triggers a CO-alarm duty (RCW 19.27.530). Low credentialing, strong disclosure — the inverse-correlation holds. But WA's true story isn't the license axis at all: it's **RCW 70A.15**, the Clean Air Act, which makes selling a new, unapproved woodstove **illegal** and hands **Ecology plus regional clean-air agencies** the power to ban wood burning outright on bad-air nights. That environmental overlay — absent from every eastern launch state — is the page's real hook: in Washington the flue is regulated less as a contractor question than as an **air-quality** one.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Washington?
faq.a: State licensing: NO state license — L&I registration (bond + insurance, NO exam), RCW 18.27. Registration or credential: YES — L&I contractor registration ($30k GC / $15k specialty bond; specialties incl. Masonry [chimney cleaning and repair] and Wood/pellet and gas stove). Seller disclosure at sale: YES — Form 17, RCW 64.06.020, asks about woodstove/insert/pellet stove/fireplace + EPA certification; chimney listed as structural item (waivable except Environmental). Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (RCW 63.14.154 + FTC). Carbon monoxide alarm law: broad + point-of-sale duty (RCW 19.27.530). Where to check a contractor: lni.wa.gov (Verify a Contractor). Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.

(woodstove, fireplace insert, pellet stove, fireplace) and, if yes, "are all of the (1) woodstoves or (2) fireplace inserts certified by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency as clean burning appliances…?"; chimneys are a listed structural component for defects, and the form asks whether the property has CO alarms, noting the seller's RCW 19.27.530 duty.

faq.a: The Consumer Protection Act, RCW ch. 19.86, gives a private action for actual damages, costs, and attorney's fees, with discretionary treble damages capped at $25,000 (RCW 19.86.090) — a softer multiplier than MA/NJ. Enforced privately and by the AG's Consumer Protection Division.
